# SPD-082 — Give the resume its own event kind member.resumed: migration 0003, kernel.EVENT_KINDS, and the six user_version assertions it moves

## Brief
SPD-050 makes a resumed spudagent count as live again, but the resume rides on the member.started event (data resumed/was_stopped_at/cleared) instead of a kind of its own, because a new kind reaches four files and four test modules no member of wave 1 owns. Giving it the kind would make spud events --kind member.resumed work, keep member.started meaning "a member started", and let the SubagentStop hold key on a kind rather than a data flag. It is cosmetic, not correctness: everything SPD-050 asked for works today.

Evidence: The work, all of it known and mechanical. (1) bin/spudlib/state/schema.py: a DDL_0004 that rebuilds the events table with member.resumed added to the kind CHECK, exactly as DDL_0002 did for the seven project and session kinds (SQLite cannot alter a CHECK); MIGRATIONS gains it and SCHEMA_VERSION = len(MIGRATIONS) becomes 4. (2) bin/spudlib/core/kernel.py EVENT_KINDS gains the string, which cli/cliparser.py turns into the --kind choices. (3) bin/spudlib/hooks/recording.py: RESUME_KIND, at the top of the resume comment block, flips from "member.started" to "member.resumed"; nothing else in recording.py or subagent_stop.py changes, since last_resume already queries by RESUME_KIND, and the resume then needs its own event beside the plain member.started rather than replacing it. (4) the version assertions move from 3 to 4: tests/test_init.py, tests/test_backup.py (two), tests/test_migrate_projects.py (two, and the fixture that migrates from 1), tests/test_hooks.py. (5) tests/test_hooks_resume.py asserts the kind of the resume event, which is written against RESUME_KIND rather than a literal. Operationally: the merge of a SCHEMA_VERSION bump makes every spud command refuse until spud migrate runs, so the merge and the migrate share one Bash line.

SPD-096 took 0003_parked on 2026-09-16 and moved every one of those assertions from 2 to 3 already, so this ticket's numbers are each one higher than the proposal said and its line numbers have shifted; read the files rather than trusting line numbers. SPD-096 also made apply_migrations follow SQLite's table-rebuild recipe (foreign keys off before BEGIN, foreign_key_check inside the transaction so a bad copy rolls back) and gave DDL_0002 its own view drops, because apply_migrations re-runs the newest VIEWS_AND_TRIGGERS after every migration and a later migration's view can name a column an earlier one has not added yet. So a rebuild of events now has a worked example two migrations deep to copy: tests/test_migrate_parked.py.
